subtopic: The Argand Plane and Polar Representation
title: De Moivre's theorem and cube roots of unity

board_content.text: So $z^{n}=r^{n}(\cos n\theta+i\sin n\theta)$ for integer $n$ — raise the modulus, multiply the angle.
This makes powers trivial: far faster than the binomial theorem.

board_content.caption: Cube roots of unity: an equilateral triangle

board_content.text: The roots of $z^{3}=1$ sit equally spaced on the unit circle, one vertex at $1$.

segments_english.text: Once multiplication adds arguments, repeated multiplication is just repeated adding, and that gives De Moivre's theorem.
De Moivre says: cosine theta plus i sine theta, all to the power n, equals cosine n theta plus i sine n theta, for any integer n.
So for a general number, z to the n equals r to the n times cosine n theta plus i sine n theta. You raise the modulus to the power and simply multiply the angle by n.
This turns hard powers into one line. Raising a complex number to the tenth or twentieth power by the binomial theorem is painful; in polar form it's immediate.
A beautiful application is the cube roots of unity: the three solutions of z cubed equals one, which sit as an equilateral triangle on the unit circle.
The non-real one, called omega, is cosine two pi over three plus i sine two pi over three, which equals minus one half plus root three over two, times i.
Two facts you'll use constantly: omega cubed is one, and one plus omega plus omega squared is zero.
Geometrically that zero-sum is obvious: three equally spaced arrows on the unit circle, one hundred twenty degrees apart, cancel out perfectly. One vertex sits at one.

segments_hinglish.text: Jaise hi multiplication arguments add karta hai, repeated multiplication bas repeated adding hai, aur ye deta hai De Moivre's theorem.
De Moivre kehta hai: cosine theta plus i sine theta, poora to the power n, barabar cosine n theta plus i sine n theta, kisi bhi integer n ke liye.
To general number ke liye, z to the n barabar r to the n times cosine n theta plus i sine n theta. Modulus ko power tak raise karo aur angle ko bas n se multiply karo.
Ye mushkil powers ko ek line bana deta hai. Complex number ko tenth ya twentieth power tak binomial theorem se raise karna painful hai; polar form mein turant.
Ek khoobsurat application hai cube roots of unity: z cubed equals one ke teen solutions, jo unit circle par equilateral triangle ki tarah baithte hain.
Non-real wala, jise omega kehte hain, hai cosine two pi over three plus i sine two pi over three, jo barabar minus one half plus root three over two, times i.
Do facts jo aap lagataar use karoge: omega cubed one hai, aur one plus omega plus omega squared zero hai.
Geometrically ye zero-sum obvious hai: unit circle par teen equally spaced arrows, one hundred twenty degrees apart, perfectly cancel ho jaate hain. Ek vertex one par baithta hai.
